node.title: Ideal-level Galois multiplicity exclusion for dyadic moment windows
node.statement: For n=2^m, an odd prime p, and a subset S of Z/n with nonzero first cyclotomic moment, divisibility by p of the first-(w-1)-moment ideal forces p^{|Z_w^odd|} to divide the first-moment norm, while that norm squared is at most (|S|-a_{n/2}(S))^{n/2}. Hence ceil((w-1)/2)log_2(p) <= (n/4)log_2|S| is necessary for a finite-characteristic accident. Periodic S reduce exactly to smaller dyadic instances; arbitrary windows require the printed per-stratum test, while for power-of-two w the top test propagates through every nonstructural stratum. The result is rowwise in p, not q=p^e.
